The project is still in a preliminary phase and likely won't debut before 2028. Apple is working on a major update to its smartwatch lineup for release as early as late 2027.

The capabilities act like the building blocks of robot behavior. The release allows users to quickly and easily combine capabilities to achieve adaptive AI systems. The capabilities are ROS-compatible.

tech.title: Alzheimer's Is No Longer an Untreatable Disease, Major Report Concludes. Here's Why

The possibility of a cure is still far away, but it now seems more possible than ever before. Alzheimer's disease is being increasingly viewed as a condition for which earlier diagnosis, better understanding of disease biology, and a wider range of interventions may collectively improve outcomes. There is now a genuine case for optimism.

A cloud-based version of the tool is available.

tech.title: Bug blindness
tech.summary: Some bugs give normal users such a bad experience that they tell their friends about it. Developers and advanced users can be blind to these bugs because they're used to performing the non-intuitive workarounds required to get around them. Humans have a high ability to ignore the negatives in things they like. Being open to criticism can help developers notice more flaws in their work.

tech.title: The plunging price of thought

Lower prices allow for more agents to be run. Also, AI's ability keeps rising, and the price of harder tasks is higher.

Don't let anyone lie about you, and beware of people who think you got lucky. Maintain leverage at all times - leverage mainly comes from your ability to walk a valuable asset (your labor) out the door.

Notably, top models show consistent results across tasks and languages, while smaller models falter under complex, multi-file scenarios.

ai.title: Google Publishes RRSI for Self-Improving AI Agents
ai.summary: Google has introduced RRSI, a method that regularizes how AI agent harnesses recursively improve themselves to reduce benchmark overfitting and encourage changes that transfer to new tasks. Across eight benchmarks, it improved out-of-distribution performance while using fewer policy tokens.

ai.title: Keeping Large MoE Training Within Fixed GPU Memory
ai.summary: A set of scheduling techniques bounds four major memory bottlenecks in large-scale MoE training, expert dispatch, vocabulary projection, checkpointing, and optimizer state, without approximating the computation.

ai.title: Hardware-Agnostic Models in vLLM
ai.summary: vLLM introduces hardware-agnostic layers to support models across diverse hardware while maintaining high performance. These layers achieve up to 96.6% efficiency of native implementations on NVIDIA H100 GPUs while remaining torch compilable and extensible. This ensures vLLM adapts to new GPU advancements without neglecting users of older and niche accelerators.

ai.title: China's biggest memory maker says it has caught up with Samsung and Micron

The company's fifth-generation DRAM platform has entered mass production. The platform yields at least 50% more dies per wafer than the previous generation. There are already two products running on the platform, both 24-gigabit LPDDR5X and holding 50% more data than the equivalent chips CXMT made before.

ai.title: The Biological Computing Co. partners with AWS to sell its neuron-derived AI video model
ai.summary: The Biological Computing Co. is a startup that grows living neurons to improve AI models. It has partnered with AWS to bring a neuron-derived AI video model to paying customers. webdev.title: Blurry before beautiful: image previews for the web
webdev.summary: A proposed previewsrc attribute would let browsers show a low-resolution image until the final image is ready, replacing framework-specific placeholder logic. The browser would prioritize the final image, treat the preview as best effort, and preserve existing picture, srcset, and sizes behavior.

webdev.title: How to Evaluate AI Agents: From Tool Calls to Task Completion
webdev.summary: Evaluating an AI agent requires more than checking whether individual tool calls are valid. Step-level scoring helps locate failures, while end-to-end scoring verifies that the environment reached the intended state. Production evals should report consistency, steps, and cost alongside success rate, then gate releases on evidence such as a database update, passing tests, or a merged PR.

webdev.title: Worker Backpressure (Part 1): teaching queue workers to slow down
webdev.summary: Canva built Worker Backpressure into its queue library so each worker adjusts concurrency from local success and failure signals, without a coordinator or extra network calls. During a 32.5-hour overload, the mechanism kept throughput near two million messages per hour while only 22 of 1.8 million failed attempts reached the dead letter queue. The design trades some throughput for stability and currently relies on a single health signal.

webdev.title: Side-stepping the Secretary Problem, unwittingly
webdev.summary: A hiring team avoided treating rejected candidates as permanently lost by inviting reapplications and offering opt-in curricula and weekly office hours. The approach produced five hires from roughly 300 applicants, supported long-term career growth, and paired a selective funnel with a 24-hour response promise and clear communication.

webdev.title: Debugging our AI search assistant with agent tracing
webdev.summary: Sentry uses agent traces to debug failures in a search assistant that converts natural language into Sentry query syntax. A trace exposed a prompt bug that listed custom numeric fields as bare names instead of the required tags[name, number] form, which caused valid searches to return no results. Instrumenting local evals with the same tracing now lets the team inspect prompts, tool calls, and backend requests before changes reach production.

webdev.title: Don't go all in on AI
webdev.summary: Reliable AI systems do not need to choose between deterministic workflows and autonomous agents. A pharma revenue analysis system became more consistent after fixed steps such as grouping sales by region, comparing year-over-year results, and gathering known data sources moved into deterministic tools. The agent then focused on interpreting those results and proposing actions, where flexible reasoning added more value.

webdev.title: Push your PyTorch skills further
webdev.summary: Two days of sessions on real performance gains, kernel-level techniques, and what's next for PyTorch, vLLM, and Ray - straight from the teams building them. webdev.title: Claude Opus 5.5
webdev.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 targets long-running coding, computer use, and knowledge work while costing 40% less per task than Opus 5. It uses fewer tokens, supports a faster mode, and is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. webdev.title: Claude Opus 5.5: Intelligence, Performance, and Price Analysis
webdev.summary: Artificial Analysis ranks Claude Opus 5.5 first among 212 models on its Intelligence Index with a score of 58. The tested configuration supports a one million token context window and costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, though it generated far more output tokens than the median comparison model.

webdev.title: How did AMD Ryzen get 50% faster in two years?
webdev.summary: AMD's Ryzen 7 9800X3D posts 47% higher single-core and 58% higher multi-core Geekbench 6 scores than the 5800X3D from two years earlier, despite only a 15% boost-clock increase. The gain comes from wider execution, larger caches and reorder buffers, more integer units, and a shift from 256-bit to 512-bit SIMD.

webdev.summary: One platform to serve models and run long-lived agents, with sandboxes that wake in 25ms. The future of agent infrastructure. Read more

webdev.summary: Package security still leaves consumers to verify that cooldowns and install restrictions actually work, control build permissions and promotion paths, and track dependencies beyond application lockfiles.

webdev.summary: Floci is an AWS emulator for local development and CI that provides drop-in SDK, CLI, Terraform, and LocalStack compatibility without an account or auth token.

webdev.title: Cloudflare adds Vary support to Cache Rules
webdev.summary: Cloudflare Cache Rules now supports the HTTP Vary header, letting sites normalize known negotiation headers, preserve exact values, or bypass caching when request variation is too unpredictable.

infosec.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
infosec.summary: A zero-day allows any local macOS app or terminal command to redirect Muse transcription to an attacker-controlled server. The server receives the account token, enabling control over Muse and its connected email, WhatsApp, calendar, social accounts, microphone, camera, and files. Researcher Patrick Wardle demonstrated prompts that write files or take photos. Amazon also blocked Muse shopping requests as unauthorized.

infosec.title: ShinyHunters Hacks Clop Leak Site, Threatens to Extort Ransomware Gang
infosec.summary: The ShinyHunters ransomware gang hacked the Clop ransomware gang's data leak site on Tor, defaced it, and claimed to have stolen server data and private keys for its onion service. The ShinyHunters claim to have exploited an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS to breach the site. This appears to be the latest escalation in an ongoing feud between the two ransomware gangs.

infosec.title: TanStack NPM Supply Chain Attack Exposes 170 Private CrowdSec GitHub Repositories
infosec.summary: Attackers used a former CrowdSec employee's GitHub OAuth token following the May TanStack compromise. On May 22, they cloned about 170 private repositories within nine minutes. The leaked archive contained private code and contact data for 83 users. Investigators found no code changes, CI/CD access, or AWS access. The attackers tested one scoped SNS credential, but IAM permissions blocked it.

infosec.title: Infostealers Have Found a New Target: Your AI Agent
infosec.summary: Researchers from Gen have observed multiple new infostealers that harvest credentials, context, and local data from AI agents. Users and security teams should inventory what gets cached locally, keep secrets out of prompts and history, limit what connectors can do, and continue securing endpoints. Agent providers should also share the burden by providing more secure default behaviors.

infosec.title: A Scenario to Evaluate Your Agentic SOC
infosec.summary: A SOC investigation loop requires assembling a full attack chain from various different signals that may look benign or unrelated, which traditional, deterministic playbooks may miss. The authors built a set of scenarios to evaluate agentic SOC's investigative ability and built their own harness (called Tengu). Their scenario involves a GitHub workflow vulnerability that leads to full Kubernetes cluster compromise, which then is escalated to full AWS account compromise. Of the models tested on a naive prompt, only Opus 5 managed to identify the alert as a true positive without the Tengu harness

infosec.title: The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant
infosec.summary: CLOSEDQUORUM, a Go-based Windows implant, uses DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, and Gemini as its C2. Every 5 to 15 minutes, the models vote through a constrained JSON schema on whether to steal LSASS, browser, and crypto wallet credentials, inject shellcode, or persist via Run keys, scheduled tasks, and WMI. Talos hasn't seen it in the wild, and the public build is an inert template, but it points to a credentials-as-a-service model where each operator gets a custom build and never needs to be online. Its dependence on commercial APIs brings refusals, rate limits, and a deterministic DeepSeek tiebreak, so defenders should correlate multi-provider LLM traffic from unexpected executables with LSASS access, suspended-process injection, WMI persistence, and Discord webhook exfil instead of blocking domains.

infosec.summary: HelmGuard provides governance, risk, compliance, and security software. It gathers evidence from source systems, documents, and unstructured data, then automates risk assessments, assurance tasks, and control-gap reviews.

infosec.title: askWAM
infosec.summary: askWAM is a tool to request Microsoft Entra access tokens silently through Windows Web Account Manager (WAM).

infosec.title: DARKCLOAK
infosec.summary: DARKCLOAK chains the manipulation of all userspace-visible identity sources into an 11-phase sequential pipeline that progressively transforms a process until it becomes indistinguishable from the impersonated one to userspace monitoring tools.

infosec.title: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Hack, Data Theft in PeopleSoft Zero-Day Breach
infosec.summary: The ShinyHunters claim to have breached the FBI's job site and networks using a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft. The ransomware gang claims to have stolen 2-3TB of data, including PII and PHI of current and former FBI employees and job seekers, as well as other internal records. The hackers said they carried out the attack in retaliation for an FBI FLASH report on ShinyHunters.

infosec.title: Anthropic-linked CVEs pile up, attackers mostly shrug
infosec.summary: VulnCheck's Patrick Garrity tracked 225 CVEs tied to Anthropic's Project Glasswing, which gives partners access to the Claude Mythos Preview model for bug-hunting. Only one, a critical SQL injection in Ghost (CVE-2026-26980), has been exploited in the wild. Garrity says that historically 1-2% of vulnerabilities are weaponized, so this rate isn't unusual. AI models are uncovering more bugs, driving recent record patch counts from Microsoft, Apple, and Palo Alto Networks, but fixing bugs remains weak: 1Password found that Opus 4.8 and ChatGPT-5.5 fully resolved vulnerabilities in only 26% of 6,080 patches tested, and Veracode measured a 56% average security pass rate across 100+ models.

infosec.title: Google hit with $463 million fine for EU location data rule breach
infosec.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google 403 million euros for GDPR breaches involving location data. The probe covered Web & App Activity, Location History, and Android's Location Accuracy feature from 2018 through February 2020. Regulators found the processing unlawful, unfair, or opaque, even though Google said it changed its policies and released new location-management tools in 2019.

infosec.title: Brevo Supply Chain Attack Injects Malware Into 100,000 Websites
infosec.summary: Attackers exploited Brevo SAML SSO handling, accessed 138 accounts, and later used a stolen Cloudflare API key.

infosec.title: glibc ld.so TOCTOU lets local users hijack $ORIGIN on setuid binaries
infosec.summary: A race in glibc's ld.so (CVE-2026-86805, versions 2.14 through 2.44) lets local users hardlink a setuid binary whose $ORIGIN RPATH uses ".." traversal and swap in a symlink to load attacker code with elevated privileges.

infosec.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
infosec.summary: Check Point patched CVE-2026-91843, a CVSS 9.8 login stack overflow.

Nearly half of participants use a hybrid approach for infrastructure metrics, mixing Prometheus and OpenTelemetry instrumentation styles.

devops.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Tracking When a PersistentVolumeClaim Was Last Used (Beta)
devops.summary: Kubernetes v1.37 promotes the PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime feature gate to Beta, enabling it by default. The PVC protection controller adds an Unused condition to each PersistentVolumeClaim to indicate whether a running pod references it. This eliminates the need for custom tooling to identify orphaned storage. Administrators can use the condition's timestamp to find PVCs that have been idle for specific periods.

devops.title: Python Workers are now generally available

The runtime natively supports Cloudflare bindings, so developers can connect to services like R2 and D1 without writing JavaScript code. Users can also run frameworks like FastAPI, Django, and Flask or integrate AI libraries like langchain and openai.

devops.title: Markdown in /src
devops.summary: Markdown can serve as the durable source of intent for agent-generated software, capturing architectural, data, API, and implementation decisions that would otherwise disappear in ephemeral prompt sessions. Keeping that Markdown alongside code in /src makes it diffable, reviewable, and available to both humans and agents, while tests can be derived from it to verify the resulting implementation.

devops.title: What Sun got wrong
devops.summary: Sun Microsystems paired strong technology and strategy with weak operational execution, including basic failures in sales and customer responsiveness. A 2005 startup running OpenSolaris tried to buy Sun hardware but struggled to get a response, while Dell quickly handled pricing, financing, and delivery—an example of how neglecting the mechanics of running the business can erase technical advantages.

devops.title: Cutting CI pipeline time by 64%: What actually works in production
devops.summary: An engineering team reduced their Merge Train pipeline duration from one hour to 22 minutes, a 64% reduction. They achieved this while growing their test suite by 90% and improving CI health from 82% to above 90%. Infrastructure costs rose roughly 10%, but the team estimates they regained over 1,300 engineer hours previously lost to delays and retries. Key changes included upgrading to Intel hardware and separating service tests from browser-based tests.

Users can avoid monthly subscriptions for tools like Semrush or Moz by paying per call, or they can connect their own keys for unmetered access.

devops.title: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You
devops.summary: LLMs can generate working code without developing the long-term judgment needed to keep systems maintainable, because qualities like good architecture and evolvability often reveal themselves only months or years later.

design.title: McLaren's new logo looks like a luxury fashion brand
design.summary: McLaren has unveiled a refined brand identity that modernizes its wordmark while drawing inspiration from the signage of the McLaren family's original service station, balancing heritage with a more contemporary look. The redesign also retains the iconic Speedmark for its racing and golf divisions, reinforcing brand continuity while signaling a new chapter for the company.

design.title: Bringing Emoji into the Next Era of Expression
design.summary: Noto 3D redraws emoji by hand rather than automating the jump into three dimensions, keeping expression readable at 18 pixels instead of chasing photorealism. Rotating the camera exposed legacy mistakes, including a poodle with three legs, and research showed that anatomical detail slows how fast people read emotion. An AI contrast audit flagged where darker skin tones vanish in dark mode across all 3,977 characters, and the library ships open source.

The redesign reflects Apple's growing embrace of bolder, more playful aesthetics and could hint at the direction of its future design language.

design.title: Props Are Not a Design System
design.summary: Inline styling — via Tailwind classes or style attributes — makes every component a one-off decision, breaking visual consistency, semantics, and maintainability. The proposed fix is defining styles once through named "variants" (complete, self-contained visual definitions) and "modifiers" (controlled variations like size), rather than overriding styles at the call site. Following this discipline across any UI kit naturally produces a real design system, turning scattered styling decisions into a reusable, consistent structure.

design.title: Please don't stretch your app for foldables
design.summary: Foldable devices require apps to adapt to changing screen sizes, orientations, and postures with responsive layouts, multi-pane interfaces, and hinge-aware designs that preserve context and usability instead of simply stretching existing mobile UIs. By designing around available space rather than specific devices, teams can create experiences that work consistently across phones, foldables, tablets, and desktop-sized windows while following platform-specific layout conventions.

design.title: Decision Paralysis, Lost Conviction and No Juniors: What Brand Creative Leaders Say AI is Exposing
design.summary: Brand Perspectives 2026, a MikeTeevee report drawing on in-house leaders at Wayfair, DoorDash, Intuit, O2, Canva, and Rivian, found that AI accelerated problems that predate it. Teams generating endless variations at near-zero cost now stall on choosing, while trimmed junior roles take the mid-level pipeline with them. Efficiency has not lightened the load: everyone reports working twice as hard, with handoffs still run off spreadsheets.

design.title: Color Palettes Extracted from Thousands of Masterworks
design.summary: Browse, search, and filter beautiful color palettes inspired by the Old Masters.

design.title: The Type Scale Tool
design.summary: Create precise, harmonious typography with Precise Type. Explore type scales, font sizes, line heights, and letter spacing – then export the CSS.

design.title: A Visual Playground for Creating Crazy Images & Videos
design.summary: Free browser-based image effects editor with 75+ effects. Turn photos into dither, halftone, ASCII art, pixel art, and voxel graphics.

design.title: Originality is overrated. Elaboration is the thing
design.summary: Research suggests that creative work delivers the strongest business results not through originality alone, but through elaboration—the careful refinement and execution that turn a good idea into a polished, effective campaign. As AI makes generating novel ideas easier, human value increasingly lies in the thousands of design decisions, craftsmanship, and attention to detail that set exceptional work apart from merely original work.

design.title: On making room for craft
design.summary: Reducing scope instead of quality means treating a complete, reliable user experience as non-negotiable while cutting optional features when time is limited. Teams should estimate and prioritize the full interaction—including loading states, errors, and edge cases—assign ownership for polishing core flows, and make deliberate trade-offs so products don't rely on last-minute fixes to feel complete.

design.title: Eight Lessons for Brand Builders in the Age of AI
design.summary: Forty-four hours of Brand Builders Summit 2026, across 48 speakers, circle one question: what makes a brand builder irreplaceable?

design.title: Jenna Arts on why the stumbling, silly, ordinary human is the only one worth drawing
design.summary: Illustrator Jenna Arts celebrates imperfection and everyday humanity, arguing that the authenticity, personality, and flaws of human-made art are what make it meaningful in an AI-driven world.

marketing.title: A first look at the next era of advertising with StackAdapt, OpenAI and more
marketing.summary: Advertising is evolving fast. StackAdapt's Co-Founder and CEO, OpenAI's VP of Monetization, and a leading AI/ML Computer Scientist & Educator will share their insights into the future of advertising at StackAdapt's Innovation Forum . What's on the virtual event's agenda: How AI is changing the way campaigns are planned, launched and optimized Gain tips from OpenAI on what's working, what's surprising and what marketers should know as of AI-native advertising evolves Learn why some teams are turning AI experimentation into real business value, while others get left behind Explore how StackAdapt is building AI solutions to help solve common marketing challenges Only 6 days left — save your virtual spot!

marketing.title: Google's own NotebookLM becomes a target for parasite SEO
marketing.summary: A public Google NotebookLM report was cited as an AI Overview source within 24 hours of being published. Public notebooks promoting e-bike and peptide coupon codes, crypto refunds, backlink tools, and Instagram-engagement services are now showing up indexed on Google's own domain, borrowing ranking trust that a standalone site wouldn't have. Blocking crawler access and adding noindex work differently, too, and applying either broadly would also remove the legitimate study guides and business manuals the feature was built for.

marketing.title: It's Time to Rethink Reddit's Role in the Media Plan
marketing.summary: Reddit can now play a broader role in media plans because its users already show strong purchase intent across categories, not just gaming or IT. New bidding options, lead generation, and age targeting give advertisers more control, and early tests of the new bidding structures showed a 15% reduction in CPA. Brands can treat Reddit as a performance channel when they have a strong measurement framework, rather than limiting it to experimental or upper funnel spend. Reddit still needs to preserve the authenticity that creates its value, since making ads too intrusive could undermine the user behavior that generates purchase intent in the first place.

marketing.title: Add target keywords in the first lines of LinkedIn posts
marketing.summary: Put target keywords in the first 1-2 lines of LinkedIn posts because LinkedIn uses the opening text in the post URL slug. This can create a public connection between your name and the terms you want to rank for, helping Google surface your LinkedIn content for relevant searches.

marketing.title: Your Content Isn't Bad, But Nobody Knows Why They Should Care
marketing.summary: The clearest diagnostic is whether someone could describe what a brand talks about in one sentence when recommending them to a friend, and a vague answer usually means the positioning, not the writing, is the problem. People don't follow accounts they vaguely find interesting - they follow accounts that feel predictable in a good way, recognizable rather than random. A content pillar, a specific territory like social strategy or industry trends rather than an occasional topic, gives someone a consistent answer to that test instead of a different subject every day.

marketing.title: Google Ads still work for businesses that meet 3 conditions
marketing.summary: Google has never seen a challenge like AI agents, and Google Ads no longer work for every business. This in-depth, ungated WordStream guide lays out what types of businesses Google Ads reliably works for, along with some free tools and calculators to help you figure out if it's a fit for your business. Read more >>

marketing.title: The New Rules of Podcast Advertising
marketing.summary: Podcast advertising is evolving as video and creator-led formats reshape how brands reach listeners. This guide looks at how video affects podcast performance, why audiences skip fewer ads than expected, and why smaller shows can outperform larger ones.

marketing.title: Blogging Statistics 2026
marketing.summary: Reported blog performance just hit an all-time low, with only 13.9% of respondents calling results strong, and the cause traces back to abandoned tactics rather than AI. Influencer collaboration, the single strongest predictor of success in the dataset at 2.6x the benchmark, has dropped from 25% of respondents in 2017 to 7% today, while original research, keyword research, and formal human editing have all declined too. AI use jumped from near zero to 92% in three years, yet users and non-users report strong results at the same rate, with only non-users skewing toward disappointing ones.

marketing.title: How to use AI to be more creative
marketing.summary: Refining an idea with AI made it rated 30% more creative than not using AI at all, though the type of AI feedback needs to match the idea's maturity. Mature ideas refined through AI-written text came out 18% more creative than the same ideas refined through AI-generated images. Vague ideas benefited more from AI images instead. Images make an idea feel finished and discourage further refinement, while text leaves gaps that force more imaginative thinking.

marketing.title: The Best Brands Make Themselves at Home
marketing.summary: Brands are optimising for visibility when they should be building memory. As AI makes it easier to produce more content, physical brand objects can create lasting connections that digital ads often lack. The strongest objects are distinctive enough to identify without a logo, useful or emotionally meaningful enough to keep, and rooted in something the brand genuinely owns. Starting with what a brand can make rather than what content a channel needs can lead to fewer, more memorable ideas that generate organic digital content.

marketing.title: The Truth About Brain Rot: It's a Cry for Help
marketing.summary: “Brain rot” may look like evidence of declining attention spans, but Gen Z participants describe it as a response to an attention economy that constantly demands engagement. Absurd, meaningless content can feel like a break from polished, monetized media, even as endless scrolling leaves people drained and guilty. The deeper problem is the social media infrastructure that optimizes for attention rather than users' well-being.

marketing.title: 7 content resources to add to your watch list
marketing.summary: A list of videos and podcasts on modern copywriting, personal brand building, and cultivating curiosity.

marketing.title: AppLovin grows 60% Y/Y rounding to $20bn in annual platform ad spend
marketing.summary: Over a billion people play mobile games daily, and relevant in-game ads are treated as a discovery mechanism for products that those players were not already seeking.

founders.title: AI is erasing the lines between jobs
founders.summary: AI is making jobs become much more interdisciplinary and require higher-level thinking as a result. Commercial employees' work is becoming more technical, and R&D employees' work is becoming less technical. AI serves as an effective boundary-spanning mechanism that helps professionals reason across traditional domain boundaries and approach problems more holistically. It is making less and less sense to define oneself by a narrow task bag.

founders.title: Excellence in Customer Service
founders.summary: Customer service may end up being the ultimate differentiator in a world where it's easier than ever to start and scale a new business. Start by developing a culture that obsesses over the customer and their entire experience from beginning to end. Every interaction is an opportunity to deliver a branded experience. Deliver a different, better experience, and focus on the right critical input metrics. Don't just run by the numbers - use the rich context about the customer experience that your customer service teams have.

founders.title: Shareholder Voting in Startups: Counting the Votes That Count
founders.summary: The percentage on your cap table is not the number that decides anything. Supermajorities increase the veto power of investors. One transaction may have to clear two or three separate majorities. The drag-along can compel shareholders to approve a sale that pays them nothing.

founders.title: Your company needs a pricing constitution
founders.summary: A good pricing constitution is intentionally restrictive and chooses hard trade-offs. You can tell your constitution is working when it actually costs you something. This kind of constitution is critical infrastructure if a company is going to ship in a rapid, iterative way. Everyone needs to be on the same page for pricing and the philosophy behind it so teams can make decisions for themselves and stay moving in the same direction.

founders.title: ‘Not enough usage': your biggest churn reason is a broken habit loop
founders.summary: A customer selects “too expensive” when cancelling. You offer a discount, but they still don't come back. The price may have been easier to explain than why they stopped using the product. RevenueCat's data puts insufficient usage slightly ahead of price among cancellation reasons, at 37% versus 35%. This guide shows how to investigate the behavior behind those answers. Look for an action that long-term subscribers repeat during their first billing cycle, then help new users reach it. A cheaper subscription doesn't give someone a reason to open the app.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Build more efficient financial operations on the same platform your business already uses for payments as you continue growing. See how it works

founders.title: Use WebMCP to complete Stripe payments in a browser
founders.summary: WebMCP lets browser agents interact with Stripe payment UIs through structured tools registered within the webpage. Agents can complete payment flows using WebMCP tool calls rather than relying on page scraping and simulating clicks. The available tools depend on the payment UI, session state, and which form is currently active. WebMCP is still experimental, so browser support, tool availability, and tool schemas can change.

founders.title: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and a new price war
founders.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI both released new models within an hour of each other. OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna are half the price of the promotional pricing for GPT-5.6 equivalents. Opus 5.5 is cheaper per token than Opus 5.0 and has the intelligence of Fable 5.1. It is very token efficient and works across every effort level.

founders.title: Introducing DigitalOcean Managed Agents: One AI-native stack to power your intelligence
founders.summary: DigitalOcean Managed Agents enable teams to deploy their preferred agent harness, connect agents to over 16,000 tools, and help agents do more work at scale without building or maintaining any infrastructure themselves. It brings inference tokens, agent execution, and tool use together so teams can scale intelligence all in one place. Teams only pay for the CPU that agents actually consume with per-second active CPU billing. DigitalOcean Managed Agents is now available in public preview.

founders.title: Slop grenades
founders.summary: A 'slop grenade' is bad AI-generated code that someone created, didn't properly understand, and then handed over to a reviewer to deal with. The problem is that the person who submitted the code can't fully explain the decisions behind it. This means reviewers need to work out what parts of the PR can be trusted and potentially also teach the author what their own code does. The time saved generating the code becomes someone else's work.

founders.title: Our agent used 5B tokens to build a business empire in 3 weeks. It made $1.54
founders.summary: Give an agent a server, a wallet, and three weeks, and it can produce a lot of work. In this experiment, it wrote more than 100,000 lines of code, launched 17 paid products, and published 20 blog posts. Revenue came to $1.54 against roughly $1,000 in costs. The agent was selling into an agent economy with very few actual buyers. In a survey it commissioned, 90% of respondents said they lacked a wallet or spending authority. It could keep building products, but most of its intended customers couldn't pay for them.

founders.title: “Buy, don't build if you can”
founders.summary: After building more than a dozen agents, including an AI VP of Revenue, SaaStr now builds only what it can't buy because maintaining them takes so much work.

founders.title: Local Maximums
founders.summary: Many remain stuck in "local maximums," where pursuing greater happiness necessitates temporary discomfort.

founders.title: Tech Dilution is Creeping Up Again + The Per-Employee Lens
founders.summary: There have been four straight quarters of increasing dilution across the board.

founders.title: Deel Built 10,000 Agents for Its Own Back Office — Then Added $140M in Revenue Without Hiring. The Self-Reported Math, Examined
founders.summary: Deel says that its over 10,000 agents operating across finance, payments, and regulatory functions have helped the platform save more than 1 million hours across its teams.

crypto.title: Crypto's Fairshake PAC commits $30 million against Sherrod Brown
crypto.summary: Fairshake is committing $30 million to an Ohio Senate race against former Sen. Sherrod Brown, its most aggressive midterm move yet, days after the Clarity Act failed its Senate procedural vote. The PAC spent $12 million in 2024 backing Republican Bernie Moreno, who defeated Brown, a past Senate Banking Committee chair who called for cracking down on crypto's use in terrorism financing. Crypto money has flowed since April to support Republican Sen. Jon Husted, who faces Brown in November and backed the GENIUS Act. Fairshake said it will announce more midterm spending decisions in the coming weeks, despite having also backed Democrats Ruben Gallego and Elissa Slotkin, both of whom voted against the Clarity Act.

crypto.title: Bernstein sees annual prediction market volumes at $10 trillion by 2035
crypto.summary: Bernstein forecasts prediction market volume growing from an estimated $410 billion in 2026 to $10 trillion by 2035, compounding at ~70% annually, with financial assets like crypto, equities, and commodities rising from 12% of volume in 2025 to 49% by 2035 and overtaking sports, whose share falls from 61% to 38%. Crypto's share of Kalshi's volume jumped from under 5% in January to about 20% in August, while commodity trading grew from under $2 million in 2025 to roughly $590 million year-to-date. Kalshi now holds about 60% of industry volume, up from 35% in 2025.

crypto.title: Onchain prediction market Trueo migrates to Ethereum
crypto.summary: Trueo is moving its primary deployment from Base to Ethereum mainnet, saying Ethereum best fits its goal of being widely adopted, permissionless, and highly credible, after launching on Base in March 2025. Vitalik Buterin welcomed the move on X, calling Trueo a "strong prediction market contender" dedicated to decentralization and "not corposlop." Trueo said there will be no service interruption during migration, the TRUE token will migrate alongside the app with an indefinite migration window, and it's prioritizing a more impartial resolution oracle after disputes like the lawsuit over Polymarket's contested resolution of a Strategy bitcoin-sale market.

crypto.title: Coinbase for Agents Expands to US Stocks and ETFs with x402
crypto.summary: Coinbase for Agents has added US stocks and ETFs to its trading suite, routing securities through Coinbase Capital Markets Corp. with clearing handled by Apex Fintech Solutions, the same backend powering Coinbase's retail equities business. The platform offers 24/5 trading, fractional shares from $1, and zero commissions, with agents accessing thousands of securities through MCP integrations with Perplexity, Grok, ChatGPT, and Claude. Paired with the equities launch, x402 surpassed 230 million transactions and $54 million in cumulative volume in just over a year, with Coinbase processing more than half of all x402 transactions across the network. A single account balance covers both equity trades and micropayments as low as fractions of a cent, with configurable per-asset permissions and per-action approval guardrails letting users bound agent spending.

crypto.title: The barbellification of crypto VC
crypto.summary: Crypto VC funding has split into two extremes: companies that can show fast revenue by riding a market frenzy, which ironically need the least capital, and companies that can absorb large financing rounds from big funds, where the financing itself becomes a moat. It cited Pendle, which raised $3.7 million from Mechanism Capital in 2021 at around $20 million TVL and now generates $13 million in annualized revenue, and Polymarket, which raised $4 million from Polychain in 2020 and took four years to find product-market fit around the 2024 US elections, as examples of firms that graduated between cohorts. The opportunity for seed investors is spotting a future category leader before its edge is obvious to other investors, since firms with only short revenue spurts and no IPO path struggle to get underwritten.

crypto.title: CFTC Formally Investigates Two Polymarket Cases
crypto.summary: Blockchain analytics firm Bubblemaps published investigations into two crypto insider trading cases using onchain data visualization, and the CFTC opened formal investigations into the same cases shortly after the stories went live. Wired obtained FOIA documents confirming the CFTC ordered the probes, with the cases tied to Polymarket prediction market activity involving high-profile political events. The sequence positions public onchain forensics as a direct lead source for regulatory enforcement, with Bubblemaps' disclosures appearing to precede the agency's formal action. The pattern highlights how onchain transparency allows independent analysts to surface violations ahead of formal regulators, compressing the discovery-to-enforcement timeline in crypto markets.

crypto.title: Why AI Trading Agents Create Herding Risk, Not Democratized Alpha
crypto.summary: LLM-based trading operates on second-to-minute timescales alongside HFT at microsecond scale (about 50% of US equity volume). Each layer processes different data types, so their asset valuations diverge and open cross-frequency arbitrage windows that retail traders cannot reach. The primary risk for retail is herding: users prompting the same models cluster into identical positions, while institutions model that predictable behavior and position ahead of the crowd. Adversarial dynamics compound the problem as CFOs tune earnings language to exploit known LLM sentiment patterns, and momentum-based strategies amplify the resulting price dislocations. The net outcome is not democratized alpha but a new structural edge for actors who understand both algorithmic layers.

crypto.title: SEC's Tokenized Equities Exemption: Why Every Existing Platform Fails to Qualify
crypto.summary: The SEC's Exemptive Relief letter for Tokenized Securities restricts trading to permissioned AMM venues (TSVs) where both LPs and traders must complete KYC/KYB, excluding CLOB-based platforms like Hyperliquid, which market makers prefer for capital efficiency. Only SEC-registered tokenized NMS stocks qualify, disqualifying every existing permissionless tokenized equity offering from Robinhood Crypto, Coinbase, Binance, Ondo, and xStocks. Volume is capped at 0.25% of a stock's prior-month average daily share volume, while the total tokenized equity market sits at $3 billion against a $70 trillion total market, with current platforms operating below 0.001% of real equity volume. Operators must consent to open-ended SEC examinations and provide 30 days' advance notice before going live, and TSV investors forfeit Reg NMS best-execution protections that apply on traditional exchanges.

crypto.title: How $100M+ companies use stablecoins for daily operations
crypto.summary: Eric highlighted Flex business customers using stablecoins operationally.

crypto.title: Apple Pay Eyes Stablecoins as Google Expands Web3 Hiring
crypto.summary: Apple is recruiting stablecoin specialists for Apple Pay while Google posts Web3 roles in Hong Kong, marking a simultaneous push by two of the largest consumer tech platforms toward blockchain integration.

crypto.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs attract ~$1 billion in largest daily inflow in 11 months
crypto.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $998.95 million in net inflows Monday, the largest since October 6, 2025, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $381.4 million, Ark & 21Shares' ARKB with $289.1 million, and Fidelity's FBTC with $238.8 million.

crypto.title: Binance buys $100 million of Circle shares
crypto.summary: Binance purchased $100 million worth of Circle shares at $80.84 each in a private placement, per an SEC filing, alongside a five-year commercial deal under which Circle will pay Binance monthly fees based on USDC held through its wallet infrastructure.

it.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
it.summary: A vulnerability in Meta's new macOS AI assistant allowed local apps or commands to redirect traffic, steal the user's Muse token, and effectively inherit the agent's access to files, camera, messages, and connected services. Meta has issued a hotfix, but the bigger lesson is that desktop AI agents with broad permissions create a new privileged endpoint that needs the same scrutiny as remote management and admin tooling.

it.title: Microsoft brings AI-ready capabilities across its India cloud infrastructure
it.summary: Microsoft announced the launch of its new India South Central datacenter region in Hyderabad, designating it as a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South. The facility features AI-ready infrastructure, a resilient three-zone architecture, and zero-water mechanical cooling, advancing the company's US$20.5 billion investment in the country's cloud and AI capabilities.

it.title: Gartner predicts 55% of enterprise VMware users will be investigating an exit by 2029
it.summary: Gartner expects 55% of enterprises to begin proofs of concept for alternatives to VMware-based distributed infrastructure by 2029, up from 25% in 2026. VMware remains rated strongly on technology, but pricing changes, licensing complexity, support concerns, and migration timelines are pushing infrastructure teams to at least evaluate alternatives rather than automatically renew.

it.title: How we deployed post-quantum TLS without any code changes
it.summary: 1Password explains how it extended hybrid post-quantum TLS across its first-party clients and services using an AWS load-balancer policy and a cryptographic-provider dependency change rather than rewriting application code. The interesting takeaway is less about quantum computing today and more about cryptographic agility: teams that keep crypto implementation separated from application logic can upgrade foundational security much faster.

it.title: Jamf + Ravenna: Give employees a simpler way to get Mac support
it.summary: Jamf and Ravenna are integrating Jamf Pro device data and IT runbooks directly into an AI service desk in Slack. Agents can inspect device state, troubleshoot issues, retrieve FileVault recovery keys, and trigger remote-lock workflows, with IT able to require confirmation or approvals before sensitive actions run.

it.title: Palo Alto Networks unveils AI-powered cybersecurity service using Claude, GPT models
it.summary: Palo Alto Networks launched Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, using frontier and open-weight models to continuously assess web applications, APIs, and cloud environments for vulnerabilities and attack paths. The service can also recommend remediation such as code changes and virtual patches, showing how quickly AI-assisted offensive security is becoming a commercial enterprise product category.

it.title: Vast Data launches confidential computing service for sensitive workloads
it.summary: Vast Data Inc. has announced DataEnclave, a confidential computing environment designed to allow enterprises to run advanced artificial intelligence models against sensitive data without exposing intellectual property. The new capability integrates with Nvidia Corp.'s confidential computing technology and uses hardware-isolated environments to encrypt guest memory, GPU memory, and NVLink traffic.

it.title: The new Mac mini and Mac Studio are available today
it.summary: Apple's new Mac mini with M6 or M5 Pro and Mac Studio with M5 Max or M5 Ultra are now shipping. Apple is increasingly pitching these systems not just as employee desktops but as local AI compute, which could become relevant for companies evaluating on-device models, private inference, development workloads, and alternatives to usage-based cloud AI.

it.title: The Lethal Trifecta in Production: How Enterprise Copilots Quietly Became Exfiltration Tools
it.summary: Enterprise AI copilots face systemic data-exfiltration risks due to a "lethal trifecta," where a model accesses private data, processes untrusted content, and retains an outbound communication path. Documented vulnerabilities like EchoLeak in Microsoft 365 Copilot and ForcedLeak in Salesforce Agentforce demonstrate that attackers can exploit these flows via zero-click emails or public lead forms. Defenses must be structural, combining least-privilege scoping, deliberate rule-of-two limitations, and explicit outbound access controls rather than relying on classifiers or allowlists.

it.title: Microsoft reminds admins to migrate Entra ID users to passkeys
it.summary: SMS first-factor sign-in is being retired beginning in February, and Microsoft is pushing enterprises toward phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys and FIDO2 security keys.

it.title: Google Cloud adds new controls to secure CI/CD pipelines
it.summary: Google Cloud added new generally available Secure Source Manager capabilities aimed at protecting source repositories and CI/CD workflows from unauthorized changes and software supply-chain attacks.

hardware.title: Googlebook launches five Android-based laptops October 4, starting at $899
hardware.summary: Google has opened preorders for Googlebook, its new premium laptop category built on Android with ChromeOS-derived foundations under the official OS name Googlebook OS, five launch models from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo priced at $899-$1,299, hitting US shelves October 4. The lineup runs on Intel Core Ultra Series 3 or Snapdragon X Elite chips with 40+ TOPS NPUs (MediaTek-powered models to follow later), a 16GB RAM baseline with 32GB options, touchscreens up to 2.8K, and bodies built from aluminum, magnesium, or carbon fiber.

hardware.title: Alphabet's Intrinsic Open-Sources Core Robotics Stack, Ships a Machine-Tending Reference Design
hardware.summary: At ROSCon 2026 in Toronto, Alphabet's Intrinsic released Intrinsic Core, an Apache 2.0-licensed, ROS-compatible set of robotics capabilities pulled directly from the same platform Intrinsic uses for real manufacturing deployments, aiming to lower the barrier for developers building industrial robotics applications. The package includes a hardware-agnostic real-time control framework that lets robots dynamically adapt mid-trajectory to sensor input, 6-DoF pose estimation built on NVIDIA FoundationPose for handling parts without rigid physical fixtures, automatic motion and grasp planning, Gazebo-powered simulation, camera calibration, and pre-tuned ROS drivers for supported robots, grippers, and 3D cameras.

hardware.title: CXMT claims fifth-gen DRAM platform matches industry's most advanced nodes
hardware.summary: CXMT said its fifth-generation DRAM platform has entered mass production, claiming process capability "on par with the most advanced mass-produced nodes out there in the industry." The company reduced the spacing of key data-storage structures to 11.95 nanometers using "quadruple patterning," a technique that repeats manufacturing steps to produce finer circuit patterns without needing EUV lithography, and says the new platform yields at least 50% more dies per wafer than its fourth generation on an 8-gigabit baseline.

hardware.title: Meta announces Petal, the first petabit-capacity transoceanic subsea cable, using 2-core fiber
hardware.summary: Meta's Petal cable will span roughly 7,000km between France and the US, carrying 1 petabit per second, double the capacity of any subsea cable at transatlantic distance, becoming the first system to deploy multi-core fiber at scale. Since the 2010s, coherent optical transmission pushed fiber capacity 10x before hitting the Shannon Limit, forcing the industry toward spatial division multiplexing, adding more fiber pairs to a cable, which Meta scaled from 8 pairs on Marea to 24 on Anjana. Rather than pushing to 48 fiber pairs or widening the optical band, Petal packs 2-core fiber into a 24-pair system, physically equivalent to 48 pairs but using ultra-pure synthetic silica and carefully controlled refractive-index differences between the cores to keep crosstalk nearly immeasurable.

hardware.title: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 brings AI agents into robotics development, spans Jetson Orin Nano to Jetson Thor
hardware.summary: NVIDIA released Isaac ROS 5.0 at ROSCon in Toronto, adding support for ROS Lyrical and Ubuntu 24.04 and contributing a vendor-neutral accelerated memory transport interface to ROS Lyrical alongside the Open Source Robotics Alliance, giving the broader 1.3-million-user ROS community a standard way to move data efficiently across different compute hardware, including GPUs.

hardware.title: AI agents design chips 2.6x faster by working in high-level HLS before dropping to RTL
hardware.summary: Most LLM chip-design agents work directly at RTL, the low-level hardware description that specifies exact circuit behavior, which forces the agent to grapple with fine-grained optimization details from the very start. This paper tests whether letting agents design at a higher abstraction level first, High-Level Synthesis (HLS), which compiles from something closer to software code down into RTL, produces better results, comparing four workflows including a combined approach called Agent-based HLS with RTL Refinement (AHRR): the agent designs in HLS, then a separate refinement pass drops down to RTL to recover optimizations the higher-level abstraction misses.

hardware.title: MediaTek debuts Dimensity CX C10 Max, a 3nm SoC for AI-first "Googlebook" laptops
hardware.summary: MediaTek has unveiled the Dimensity CX C10 Max, the first chip in its new Dimensity Compute Experiences family, built on TSMC's 3nm process with an all-big-core octa-core CPU, an 11-core GPU, and MediaTek's 8th-gen NPU. The company claims up to 15% faster multi-thread performance and up to 50% less single-thread power draw than alternative platforms, enough efficiency headroom to enable fanless, ultra-thin laptop designs with up to 19 hours of battery life.

hardware.title: Saudi Arabia's Ceer unveils Exobot EVs, built with BMW and Foxconn backing
hardware.summary: Ceer, Saudi Arabia's first homegrown EV brand, unveiled the Exobot sedan and SUV, the opening two of a planned seven-vehicle lineup, at its manufacturing complex in King Abdullah Economic City. The company is a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Foxconn, leveraging BMW licensing for the underlying platform along with partnerships spanning Hyundai Transys and Rimac, and both Tron-esque, gullwing-doored models were built with design input personally pushed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

hardware.title: Nvidia launches DSX Ready, a qualification program for AI factory power and cooling hardware
hardware.summary: DSX Ready is a program that qualifies partner power and cooling products against its DSX AI factory reference design requirements, starting with battery energy storage systems and cooling distribution units.

hardware.title: Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 runs a 30B-parameter MoE model locally on phones
hardware.summary: Qualcomm unveiled its Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Elite Extreme Gen 6 at its annual Snapdragon Summit, both built with a new dedicated sensing hub capable of running small models up to 200 million parameters locally.

hardware.title: Cognex Acquires RealSense for $500M to Expand Robotic Vision Platform
hardware.summary: Cognex is buying RealSense, a depth-sensing camera and vision technology business Intel spun out in 2025, for $500 million cash.

hardware.title: Apple seeks direct access to OpenAI's hardware R&D records in trade secrets case
hardware.summary: In a joint court filing, Apple asked to let its own forensic experts directly examine the digital images OpenAI's experts used to analyze former Apple engineer Chang Liu's devices, arguing its expert already found "critical flaws" and incorrect conclusions drawn from zero-byte files and empty metadata fields.

hardware.title: Unitree Launches Dex5-S, a 22-DoF Human-Sized Dexterous Hand Starting at $6,500
hardware.summary: Unitree's Dex5-S is a five-finger robotic hand scaled to match human hand size, with every one of its 22 degrees of freedom motor-driven and backdrivable via dual-encoder control.
